dialog.body: Public Works, this is Kevin. Good morning, well, just about afternoon. How can I help?

Hi, Kevin, honey. Margaret Thurston calling. I'm sorry, I'm on my cell, so if I cut out you just holler. I'm calling about the storm drain in front of my house. Again, I should say, because I've been looking at that thing for years and it's never been right.
Sure, no problem. Where are you located?

370 Farewell Street, up in the North End. And I'll tell you, I've lived here a good long while and I have never once had water in my cellar. Not once. Then the rain from Friday into Saturday, two days ago, and I go down Saturday morning for a jar of tomatoes and my slippers are wet.
Oh boy. How much water are we talking?

A few inches, dear. Seeped in along the back wall. It's not up to the furnace, thank goodness, but that's a few inches I never had before. And the drain out front was just a lake. The leaves and the muck are all piled on top of the grate, and the water couldn't go anywhere, so it came up the gutter and into the yard.
Okay, so the catch basin out front is clogged with debris. Let me write that down. Three seventy Farewell, drain blocked, water into the cellar.

That's right. And here's the other thing, it's running downhill toward my neighbor's garage. He's got the one that sits low next to the driveway. I watched the water creeping right along the edge of his apron Saturday afternoon. I went over and told him, and he just shrugged, he's not one to fuss, but I'm fussing for him.
Yeah, that's worth getting on. Has it drained down any since Saturday?

[line breaks up] ...sorry, I'm in the car, I'm at one of those charging stops, so the signal's a little funny. I switched to an electric car this winter, my first one, and now I know every charger between here and Providence. Anyway, what was it? Oh, the water. Yes, it's mostly gone from the street, but the drain's still full of junk. It'll do it again with the next good rain.
Gotcha. You said you're at a charger, so is this still a good number to reach you? I've got the number you're calling from.
It's 401-555-0175. That's the cell. I don't pick up the house phone anymore, honey, it's all spam.
Okay, 401-555-0175. I'll put in a work order to have a crew come clean out that catch basin. Is the grate right in front of the house, or at the corner?
Right in front, at the curb. You can't miss it, it's the one with a little pond around it. I've called about it before, a couple of years back, I think, but it just sort of got forgotten.

I'm not seeing anything under this address in front of me, so I'll start fresh. I'll flag that water is running toward the neighbor's garage and that you got water in the cellar. That should bump it up.

Thank you. I do wish somebody would just come and clean it before the rains, instead of after. It's frustrating, you know? I pay my taxes. I'm not asking for the moon, I'm asking for a drain that drains.

No, that's fair. Crews are stretched after a storm like this, and there's a list, but a blocked basin with water at a house goes toward the top. You'll probably see somebody in the next few days, give or take.
Days. All right. And if it rains Wednesday, which I hear it might, what then?
Then call back and tell them it's the same work order, and I'll note that you called today at noon or so. Anything else down there I should know, like is the grate itself damaged, or just clogged?
Just clogged, as far as I can see. Leaves, a plastic bag, and I think a lot of sand from the winter. It's packed in there.
Okay, clogged with leaves, bag, and sand. Got it. Is there anything else going on at the house? Any sewer smell or anything coming up through the floor drain?
No, no, just the water through the wall. I've mopped it all up and I've got a fan running down there.
Good. Alright, Mrs. Thurston, I've got it all in. Cleaning request for the drain at 370 Farewell, cellar seepage, water heading toward the neighbor's garage.
Thank you, Kevin. You've been very kind, dear. I'm going to go see if this car has decided to charge.
Good luck with that. Take care.
